text:
olga: heads up — onboarding new HF fork (bert-chat-lite -> causal-chat) is slipping because the tool-calling tokens get split after our quantization pass. noticed bad json outputs in evals.

mike: ugh. is this the usual additional_special_tokens mismatch?

olga: yeah partly. HF model had: `additional_special_tokens: ['<TOOL>', '</TOOL>', '<JSON_START>', '<JSON_END>']` but tokenizer in our conversion ended up byte-pair-splitting `<JSON_START>` into `<`, `JSON`, `_`, `START`, which breaks the regex extractor in the eval harness.

raj: can you paste the config.json + tokenizer snippet? might be a simple mapping in the hf->rw script.

olga: pasting minimal snippets — note: this is the HF repo before conversion:
```json
{
  "tokenizer": {
    "model_max_length": 2048,
    "add_prefix_space": true,
    "additional_special_tokens": ["<TOOL>", "</TOOL>", "<JSON_START>", "<JSON_END>"]
  },
  "model_config": {
    "architectures": ["CausalLMForChat"],
    "bos_token": "<s>",
    "eos_token": "</s>"
  }
}
```

mike: ok. two failure modes we've seen: 1) conversion script doesn't call `tokenizer.add_special_tokens(...)` before saving -> tokenizer.json lacks them; 2) quantization pipeline (qat/ptq) does subword merging artifacts when tokenizer vocab->ids remap happens.

kevin: quantization causing split tokens? interesting — can you repro with the non-quantized fp16 model? if it's fine there, then we know it's a pipeline reorder bug.

olga: fp16 run is fine. quantized run shows split tokens and the model emits `\"{\"action\": \"open\", \"tool\": \"<`, then broken tokens.

raj: quick fixes we can try: 1) force-add role/tool/json tokens to the tokenizer pre-conversion, 2) embed token IDs in the conversion mapping so our `rw-token-mapper` preserves them, 3) adjust JSON extractor to tolerate tokenized fragments as fallback (ugly).

sara: prefer (1) + (2). adding tokens early is safest. example patch for conversion script:
```py
# conversion.py (pseudo)
new_tokens = ['<TOOL>', '</TOOL>', '<JSON_START>', '<JSON_END>', '<|system|>', '<|user|>', '<|assistant|>']
tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens': new_tokens})
model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))
# then save tokenizer and model
```

kevin: also ensure the role tokens we add match chat templates. HF chat templates often include role names inline; our Redwood runtime expects role markers like `<|assistant|>`. If mismatched, the chat formatter will produce double-role markers.

ezra: small gotcha: when we quantize with library X, it stores an order of vocab -> ids and sometimes reindexes. we should persist the `tokenizer.get_vocab()` into model card and assert `vocab_size` matches before the runtime loads weights. Add a CI check in onboarding pipeline.

olga: noted. i'll add a preflight that does `assert set(new_tokens).issubset(set(tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(range(len(tokenizer)))))`.

mike: for JSON mode: our eval harness uses `JSON_START`/`JSON_END` strings to find structured output. maybe standardize canonical tokens to `\u0006JSON_START\u0007` (unprintable sentinels) to avoid subword risk? downside: harder for humans to read logs.

raj: i'd avoid unprintable unless necessary. we can instead require that special tokens be single-token in the tokenizer. test with `tokenizer.encode('<JSON_START>')` and assert length==1. add that to onboarding checks.

olga: good call. i'll do both checks: present in vocab and single-token.

sara: regarding tool/function calling schema — reminder: tool tags in function responses must be emitted as raw tokens (not broken) because our function parser expects exact `<TOOL>...</TOOL>` wrappers. update docs: https://redwood.internal/devx/tool-calls -> include conversion hints.

eval-bot: perf-eval queued: run `json-structure-score` on new model after token fixes (job 4872).

kevin: one more wrinkle — HF uses `eos_token` as `</s>`; some chat templates terminate with eos and then append `</TOOL>` which can be tokenized together. recommend setting `eos_token=None` in tokenizer config for chat-style models or ensure special tokens are never suffix-merged.

olga: good point. i'll try `tokenizer.add_special_tokens({'eos_token': '</s>'})` explicitly and test.

mike: action items:
- olga: add tokenizer presence + single-token checks, add preflight assertion in onboarding script (1789501500 ETA)
- kevin: instrument quantization pipeline to snapshot tokenizer.get_vocab() before/after quant step (PR today)
- raj: add mapping safeguard in rw-token-mapper to preserve special token ids (will review)
- sara: update internal doc with conversion checklist and example patches

olga: thanks. i'll post results here. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: model-conversion-fix-178950 -> staging at 2026-03-20T15:42Z

olga: test run post-deploy shows `tokenizer.encode('<JSON_START>') == [50234]` (length 1) and eval JSON parse errors dropped from 22% -> 0.8%. woo! :party-parrot:

mike: excellent. leave open until CI green then ship to prod.

sara: noted. i'll close the onboarding ticket once CI jobs pass.

olga: closing loop — thanks all.
